rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which is either at-fault just cause (such as nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, or unlawful use) or no-fault just cause taken in good faith (owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order or local ordinance, or demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies (lawful right to occupy for more than 30 days, excluding fixed-term leases of three months or less) of residential rental property in San Diego, other than the exempt property types listed in section 98.0703.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable housing; housing subject to affordable housing subsidy agreements (not including Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care, licensed residential care for the elderly, adult residential facilities, non-profit transitional housing; school and higher-education dormitories; units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with a landlord who lives there; owner-occupied single-family residences (including renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs, and a mobilehome); two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupies one unit; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, if tenants were given the required written exemption notice.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §98.0704; O-21647 N.S.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.interaction_text: The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.

rules.title: Owner Move-In Just Cause Conditions
rules.requirement: An owner move-in termination applies only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and lives there for at least 12 continuous months; for leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, it applies only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it, and the notice must name the intended occupant and their relationship to the owner. If the occupancy requirements are not met, the owner must offer the unit back to the tenant at the same rent and terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses.
rules.key_value: Intended occupant must move in within 90 days and occupy for at least 12 continuous months
rules.coverage_text: Non-exempt residential rental property in San Diego where the owner seeks to recover possession for the owner or a listed family member.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the intended occupant occupies a rental unit on the property or if a vacancy of a similar unit already exists at the property. Death of the intended occupant after moving in within 90 days is not a failure to comply.
rules.penalty: Owner must offer the unit to the vacated tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses in excess of relocation assistance paid.
rules.quoted_span: (E) Section 98.0704(b)(1) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the residential rental property within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the residential rental property for at least 12 continuous months.

rules.title: Demolition or Substantial Remodel Termination Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord terminating to demolish or substantially remodel must post the permit application within three business days of submittal and secure required permits before issuing notice, and the notice must be certified under penalty of perjury and include the intent statement, the right-to-re-rent statement, a description and duration of the work with permits or contract, and why the tenant must vacate for at least 30 continuous days.
rules.key_value: Work must require the tenant to vacate for at least 30 continuous days
rules.coverage_text: Non-exempt residential rental property in San Diego where the landlord seeks possession to demolish or substantially remodel.
